p0.original: 第七章 用全身心倾听
p0.en: Chapter seven, listen to me with all your heart.

p1.original: 在前四章中，我们介绍了如何通过非暴力沟通的四个要素来表达自己。本章我们将探讨如何倾听他人，了解他们的观察、感受、需要和请求，并给予反馈。
p1.en: In the first four chapters, we describe how we express ourselves through the four elements of Nonviolent Communication. This chapter will explore how to listen to others, understand their observations, feelings, needs and requests, and provide feedback.

p2.original: 为了倾听他人，我们需要先放下已有的想法和判断，全神贯注地体会对方。以色列哲学家马丁·布伯（Martin Buber）对此作出了描述：“尽管有种种相似之处，生活的每时每刻就像一个刚出生的婴儿，一张新的面孔，我们从未见过，也不可能再次见到。我们无法停留在过去，也无法预见我们的反应。我们需要不带成见地感受变化。我们需要用全身心去倾听。”
p2.en: In order to listen to others, we need to put aside existing ideas and judgements and focus on each other. The Israeli philosopher Martin Buber described it: “Despite all the similarities, life is like a newborn baby, a new face, never seen, not again. We cannot stay in the past, nor can we anticipate our response. We need to feel change without prejudice. We need to listen with all our energy.

p3.original: 然而，用全身心倾听他人并不容易。法国作家西蒙娜·薇依（Simone Weil）写道：“倾听一个处于痛苦中的人，不仅十分罕见，而且非常困难。那简直是奇迹；那就是奇迹。有些人认为他们可以做到，实际上，绝大部分的人还不具备这种能力。”遭遇他人的痛苦时，我们常常急于提建议，安慰或表达我们的态度和感受。可是，倾听意味着全心全意地体会他人的信息——这为他人充分表达痛苦创造了条件。有一句佛教格言恰如其分地描述了这种能力：“不要急着做什么，站在那里。”
p3.en: It is not easy, however, to listen to others with all of your heart. The French writer Simone Weil writes: “Listening to a person in pain is not only rare, but also very difficult. It's a miracle. That's a miracle. Some believe that they can do this, and in fact the vast majority of people do not yet have the capacity. “We are often anxious to offer advice, comfort or express our attitudes and feelings when we experience the suffering of others. However, listening means fully understanding the message of others — which creates the conditions for others to fully express their pain. There is a Buddhist proverb that aptly describes this ability: “Don't rush to do what you are doing and stand there.

p4.original: 如果一个人想要别人了解他的处境，听到的却是安慰和建议，那么，他就有可能觉得不太舒服。我和女儿的一次对话提醒我，在安慰他人或提建议前，先看看那是否是他们想要的。有一天，我女儿在照镜子时说：“我丑得像一只猪。”
p4.en: If a person wanted someone to understand his situation and heard consolation and advice, he might feel uncomfortable. My daughter and I had a conversation that reminded me that before consoling others or making suggestions, we would see if that was what they wanted. One day, my daughter looked in the mirror and said, "I'm ugly as a pig.

p5.original: “你是世界上最美丽的女孩！”我大声宣布。女儿很不高兴地看了我一眼，喊了声“爸呀”，然后摔上门出去了。我的安慰看来不合时宜。也许，她只是希望我留意她的感受。也许当时我最好问她：“你对你今天的形象感到很失望吗？”
p5.en: "You're the most beautiful girl in the world! "I'll announce it aloud. My daughter was very unhappy to look at me and shouted "Daddy" and fell out of the door. My consolation does not seem appropriate. Maybe she just wants me to keep an eye on her feelings. Maybe I better ask her, "Are you disappointed with your image today?

p6.original: 我的朋友霍利·汉弗里（Holley Humphrey）举了一些例子，来说明哪些行为会妨碍我们体会他人的处境。
p6.en: My friend Holly Humphrey gave examples of what might prevent us from understanding the situation of others.

p8.original: ·比较：“这算不了什么。你听听我的经历……”
p8.en: • Comparative: “This is nothing. Listen to my experience..."

p9.original: ·说教：“如果你这样做……你将会得到很大的好处。”
p9.en: • Preacher: “If you do this you will have a great deal of benefit.

p10.original: ·安慰：“这不是你的错；你已经尽最大努力了。”
p10.en: • Consolation: “It's not your fault; You've done your best.

p12.original: ·否定：“高兴一点。不要这么难过。”
p12.en: • Negative: “Be happy. Don't be so sad.

p14.original: ·询问：“这种情况是什么时候开始的？”

p15.original: ·辩解：“我原想早点打电话给你，但昨晚……”
p15.en: • Defense: “I wanted to call you earlier, but last night...”

p16.original: ·纠正：“事情的经过不是那样的。”哈罗德·库希纳（Harold Kushner）拉比在《当好人遭到了厄运》一书中诉说了他的苦难。在他儿子临死时，听到人们的安慰，他极为痛苦。然而，想到20多年来他在别人遭遇不幸时也说同样的话，他更是伤透了心！
p16.en: • Correct: “This is not the way things are going. "Harold Kushner, Rabbi, told us about his suffering in the book "Being a Good Man is Accursed". When his son was dying, he heard the comfort of the people, and he suffered greatly. However, he was heartbroken to think that he had said the same thing to others for more than 20 years.

p17.original: 我们常常认为，在亲友感到痛苦时，我们应该想办法使他们好受一点。然而，急于采取行动使我们无法充分体会他们的状况。对于从事心理咨询或热线服务的人来说，更是如此。在一次研讨班中，我问23位心理医生，如果向他们求助的人说“我快要崩溃了，我找不到活下去的理由”，他们会有怎样的反应。我收集好他们的书面回答后提议：“我将依次大声读出这些书面回答。假定你是那位求助的人，如果你认为某个回答表达了对你的理解，就请你举起手来。”在23个回答中，只有3个有人举手。其中，最常见的反应是，像“这是什么时候开始的”这类的问题。也许，他们是希望通过收集足够的信息来分析和解决问题。事实上，试图分析问题妨碍了我们与他人的联系。如果我们只关心别人说了什么，并考虑他的情况符合哪种理论，我们是在诊断人——我们并没有倾听他们。在非暴力沟通中，倾听他人意味着，放下已有的想法和判断，一心一意地体会他人。倾听的这种品质体现了它与理解以及同情之间的区别。
p17.en: We often believe that when relatives and friends suffer, we should find ways to make them feel better. However, our eagerness to act does not allow us to fully appreciate their situation. This is particularly true for persons who are engaged in psychological counselling or hotline services. In one of the workshops, I asked 23 psychologists how they would react if they were to say to them, “I'm about to collapse, I can't find a reason to live”. I collected their written answers and proposed: “I will read them out loud in turn. Assume you're the one who asked for help, if you think one of the answers expresses an understanding of you, raise your hands. Of the 23 replies, only 3 were raised. Among them, the most common response is questions such as “when this began”. Perhaps they want to analyse and solve the problem by gathering enough information. In fact, attempts to analyse the problem have hampered our contacts with others. If we only care about what others say and consider what theory his situation fits, we are diagnosing people — we have not listened to them. In Nonviolent Communication, listening to others means putting aside existing ideas and judgements and understanding others with one mind. This quality of listening reflects the difference between it and understanding and compassion.

p18.original: 体会他人的感受和需要
p18.en: Feel the feelings and needs of others.

p19.original: 不论别人以什么样的方式来表达自己，我们都可以用心体会其中所包含的观察、感受、需要和请求。比方说，一位新邻居因为急事借走了你家的车。你的家人知道后责骂你：“你把车借给了陌生人，真蠢！”此时，你就可以好好体会他们的感受和需要，既不反驳也不自责。
p19.en: Whatever the way others express themselves, we can all feel the observations, feelings, needs and requests that are contained in them. For example, a new neighbor borrowed your car for an emergency. Your family scolds you after you know it: "You lent your car to strangers, stupid! At this point, you can appreciate their feelings and needs, and you can neither rebut nor blame yourself.

p20.original: 不论别人说什么，我们只听到他们此时此刻的（a）观察，（b）感受，（c）需要，和（d）请求。
p20.en: Whatever others say, we hear only their (a) observation, (b) feeling, (c) need, and (d) request at this moment.

p21.original: 在这个例子中，很明显，家人观察到的事实是：车被借给了陌生人。有的时候，别人的话基于怎样的观察，并不一目了然。例如，一位同事说：“你没有团队精神。”在这句话中，他并没有提到他的观察是什么。我们需要通过询问来了解我们的猜测是否准确。
p21.en: In this example, it is clear that the family observed the fact that the car was lent to strangers. Sometimes others say things based on what observation they see. For example, one colleague said, “You have no team spirit. In this sentence, he does not mention what his observations are. We need to ask whether our guess is accurate.

p22.original: 有位女士和她先生的交流出现了一些困难。她先生对她说：“和你说话有什么用？你从不好好听。”我给她的建议是，她先猜猜先生的感受和需要，然后，再回去和先生谈。在下面的对话中，我试着帮助这位女士做到这一点。
p22.en: There were some difficulties in communicating with a woman and her husband. Her husband said to her, "What's the point of talking to you? You never listen. My advice to her was that she would guess what he felt and needed and then go back and talk to him. In the dialogue that follows, I have tried to help the woman do so.

p23.original: （先生：“和你说话有什么用？你从不好好听。”）
p23.en: "What's the point of talking to you, sir? You never listen. The blogger says:

p24.en: Ma'am, are you mad at me?

p25.original: 马歇尔：“你这么说，意味着他生气是由于你的缘故。我建议你说，‘你不高兴，是因为 你需要……’这有助于你去了解他此刻的状态，而避免责备自己。”
p25.en: Marshall: "You say that means he's angry because of you. I suggest you say, "You're not happy because you need..." to help you understand what he's doing at the moment and avoid blaming yourself.

p26.original: 太太：“但我说什么呢？‘你不高兴，是因为你需要……’需要什么？”
p26.en: "Madam, but what am I saying? "You're not happy because you need..." What do you need?

p27.original: 马歇尔：“从你先生的话中去寻找线索。他说，‘和你说话有什么用？你从不好好听’。当他那样说的时候，他没有得到什么？”
p27.en: Marshall: "Go look for clues from your husband. He said, "What's the point of talking to you? You never listen. When he said that, he didn't get anything?

p28.original: 太太：（试图体会先生的需要）“你感到不高兴，是因为你觉得我不理解你？”
p28.en: Mrs. M.: "You're upset because you think I don't understand you?

p29.original: 马歇尔：“你现在关心的是他的想法而非他的需要。我想，如果我们注意的是别人的需要而非他对我们的看法，我们将发现别人并不那么可怕。我们还会发现，他不高兴是因为他的需要没有得到满足。”
p29.en: Marshall: You're now concerned with his ideas, not his needs. I think that if we are paying attention to the needs of others rather than to what he thinks of us, we will find others not so terrible. We will also find him unhappy because his needs have not been met.

p30.original: 太太：（再试一次）“你不高兴是因为你需要得到理解？”
p30.en: Madam: "You're not happy because you need to understand?

p31.original: 马歇尔：“这正是我想到的。你觉得这和你之前的表达有什么不同吗？”
p31.en: Marshall: That's what I thought. Do you think that's different from what you said before?

p32.original: 太太：“当然，很大的不同。我把注意力放在了他现在需要什么，而不是自己做错了什么。”
p32.en: Ma'am: Of course, it's a big difference. I focused on what he needed now, not what he did wrong.

p34.original: 在倾听他人的观察、感受、需要和请求之后，我们可以主动表达我们的理解。如果我们已经准确领会了他们的意思，我们的反馈将帮助他们意识到这一点。反之，如果我们的理解还不到位，他们也就有机会来纠正我们。此外，这样做还有助于人们体会自己的状况，从而深入了解自己。
p34.en: Having listened to others ' observations, feelings, needs and requests, we can express our understanding on our own initiative. If we have already understood their meaning precisely, our feedback will help them to realize that. On the contrary, if we do not have an understanding, they will have an opportunity to correct us. In addition, it helps people to understand their own situation and thus gain insight into themselves.

p35.original: 非暴力沟通建议我们使用疑问句来给予他人反馈。这将便于他人对我们的理解作出必要的补充。我们的问题可以集中于以下几个方面：
p35.en: Nonviolent Communication suggests that we use the question phrase to give feedback to others. This will allow others to supplement our understanding as necessary. Our problems can be concentrated on the following areas:

p36.original: 1.他人的观察：“上周我有三个晚上不在家，你说的是这回事？”
p36.en: “I was away three nights last week, and you said that?

p37.original: 2.他人的感受及需要：“你很灰心？你希望得到肯定是吗？”
p37.en: “You're frustrated? Do you want to be sure?

p38.original: 3.他人的请求：“你是不是想请我帮你预订酒店？”
p38.en: “Do you want me to book your hotel?

p39.original: 请注意上述问题与以下问题的区别：
p39.en: Please note the difference between the above issues and the following:

p41.original: 2.“你现在心情怎么样？”“为什么你会有那样的感觉？”
p41.en: “How are you feeling now? "Why do you feel that way?"

p42.en: “What do you want me to do?

p43.original: 第二组问题并不需要我们用心体会他人。这些问题看起来很直接，但根据我的经验，它们并不是获得信息的最佳方式。这样的提问方式，就像心理咨询师在帮助客户，容易产生距离感。如果我们真的要这么问，那么，在提问前先提及我们的感受和需要，将鼓励人们主动表达自己。例如，如果我们想问别人“你说的是什么事”，我们可以说：“我有些困惑。我想知道你是指哪件事。告诉我好吗？”虽然，这并不是必要的——有时，我们的语气已经表明了我们的感受和需要；但我还是建议主动表达感受和需要，特别是情绪很激烈的时候。
p43.en: The second set of issues does not require us to be sensitive to others. These questions seem straightforward, but in my experience they are not the best way to obtain information. This way of asking questions is like the way that a psychologist is helping a client, which can easily create a sense of distance. If we really ask that, then mentioning our feelings and needs before asking them will encourage people to express themselves. For example, if we want to ask someone what you're saying, we can say, “I'm a little confused. I want to know what you mean. Will you tell me? “Although this is not necessary — sometimes our tone has shown our feelings and needs; But I suggest that I be proactive in expressing feelings and needs, especially when emotions are strong.

p44.original: 什么时候需要给别人反馈呢？首先，在对自己的理解没有把握时，我们需要对方的确认。然而，即使确信自己已经明白了，我们可能还会发现别人正期待我们的反馈。有时，人们甚至会直接问：“我的意思清楚吗？”或“你明白我的意思吗？”这时，简单回答“是的，我明白了”可能是不充分的，人们也许期待我们说得具体些。
p44.en: When do you need to give feedback? First of all, we need confirmation from the other side when our understanding is uncertain. However, even if we are certain that we have understood, we may find that others are expecting our feedback. Sometimes people even ask, "Do I mean it? Or "Do you understand what I mean?" At this point, the simple answer is “Yes, I understand” may not be sufficient and one may expect us to be more specific.

p45.original: 一位女士在参加非暴力沟通研讨班后不久，到一个医院当了义工。一些护士请她去和一位老太太谈话。护士们告诉她：“我们和她说，她的病并不重，只要吃药，病情就会好转。可是，她听不进去，整天坐在屋子里喃喃自语‘我不想活了’，‘我不想活了’。”这位女士见到老太太时，就像护士们说得那样，她独自坐在房中，不停地说“我不想活了”。
p45.en: Shortly after attending a workshop on Nonviolent Communication, a woman was a volunteer at a hospital. Some nurses asked her to talk to an old lady. The nurses told her, "We told her she was not very sick, and if she took her medication, she would get better. But she couldn't hear it, and she sat in the house all day saying, "I don't want to live anymore," "I don't want to live anymore." “When she met the old lady, as the nurses said, she sat alone in her room and kept saying, “I don't want to live”.

p46.original: “你的意思是你不愿意活下去了？”这位女士问老太太。老太太很惊讶，停了下来，表情也轻松多了。她开始讲，从没有人知道她是多么痛苦。这位女士继续表达她的理解。很快，她们就感受到彼此的情意，手挽手地坐在一起。当天晚些时候，老太太就开始吃饭、服药，情绪也明显好转。尽管护士们一直在安慰老太太并给她建议，但只有这位女士为老太太提供了她真正需要的东西——她需要有人能理解她深深的绝望。
p46.en: "You mean you don't want to live? The lady asks the old lady. The old lady was surprised, stopped, and her face was much easier. She began by saying that no one ever knew how painful she was. The woman continued to express her understanding. Soon they felt each other's feelings and sat together with their hands. Later in the day, the old lady began eating and taking medication, and her emotions improved markedly. Although the nurses have been comforting and advising the old lady, only the woman has provided her with what she really needs — she needs someone to understand her deep despair.

p47.original: 一般来说，如果一个人在说话时有明显的情绪，他一般会期待得到他人的反馈。如果我们自己是说话的那个人，我们不妨清楚地表明我们是否期待反馈。
p47.en: In general, if a person speaks with a clear emotion, he generally expects feedback from others. If we are the one who speaks for ourselves, we may wish to make it clear whether we expect feedback.

p48.original: 然而，在一些文化环境中，我们也许很难用语言给他人反馈。有一位来自中国的先生在过去常常从父亲的话中听到责骂和攻击。为此，他很害怕去见父亲，每隔几个月才硬着头皮去一次。为了改善与父亲的关系，他参加了非暴力沟通研讨班。十年后，他告诉我，听到父亲的责骂时，他现在总是努力静下来体会父亲的感受和需要。因此，父子关系已变得十分亲密。可是，他从没有说出他所意识到的父亲的感受。他解释说，“在我们的文化中，直接谈论一个人的感受是很少见的。重要的是，我已经不再把他的话看作是对我的攻击，而注意体会他的感受和需要。这使我们的关系日益好转。”
p48.en: However, in some cultural settings, it may be difficult for us to give back language to others. A Mr. from China had heard in the past, often from his father, verbal abuse and attacks. As a result, he was afraid to see his father and only went every few months under his skin. In order to improve his relationship with his father, he participated in a workshop on Nonviolent Communication. Ten years later, he told me that when he heard his father's scolding, he was now trying to calm down and feel his father's feelings and needs. As a result, paternity has become very close. However, he never said what his father felt as he realized. He explained, “It is rare in our culture to talk directly about one's feelings. It is important that I no longer see his words as an attack on me, but that I take care of his feelings and needs. This has led to a growing improvement in our relations.

p49.original: 我问道：“你的意思是说，你将永远不会和你父亲提他的感受，但留意他的感受对改善你们的关系十分重要？”
p49.en: I asked, “You mean you'll never talk to your father about his feelings, but it's important to keep an eye on his feelings to improve your relationship?

p50.original: “不。我想现在大概可以了。我们的关系这么好，如果我和他说‘爸，你现在很伤心吗’，我想他不会觉得意外。”他回答说。
p50.en: “No. I think it's probably all right now. We were so close, if I told him, "Daddy, are you sad now?" I don't think he'd be surprised. He replied.

p51.original: 在给他人反馈时，我们的语气十分重要。一个人在听别人谈自己的感受和需要时，将会留意其中是否暗含着批评或嘲讽。如果我们的语气很肯定，仿佛是在宣布他们的内心世界，那么，通常不会有好的反应。然而，一旦别人通过我们的语气意识到我们是在体会，而非下结论，他们一般就不会产生反感。
p51.en: Our tone is very important in giving feedback to others. A person who listens to others about his or her feelings and needs will be mindful of whether there is any implicit criticism or ridicule. If our tone is very positive, as if it were to proclaim their inner world, then there will normally be no good response. However, once others realize through our tone that we are understanding, not drawing conclusions, they will not generally be repulsive.

p52.original: 有时，我们的意图可能会被误解。人们也许说：“不要用沟通技巧来套我的话。”如果出现这种情况，我们可以继续倾听对方的感受和需要。这时，我们也许会发现，对方并不信任我们，除非对我们的意图有进一步的了解，他不会喜欢我们表达的方式。然而，就像上文的例子所反映的，只要我们专注于他人的感受和需要，所有的批评、攻击、辱骂或嘲讽就会消失。我们越是这样做，就越能体会到一个简单的事实：有时，我们认为自己受到了指责，实际上，那些话是他人表达需要和请求的方式。如果意识到这一点，我们就不会认为自己的人格受到了伤害。反之，如果一心分析自己或对方的过错，我们就会认为自己被贬低了。作家约瑟夫·坎伯（Joseph Campbell）说道：“为了幸福，必须把‘别人怎么看我’这个问题放在一边。”一旦我们把所谓的批评和指责看作是来自他人的礼物——为处于痛苦中的人提供服务的机会，我们就会感到这种幸福。
p52.en: Sometimes our intentions may be misunderstood. One might say, "Don't use communication skills to trap my words. If that happens, we can continue to listen to each other's feelings and needs. At that point, we may find that the other side does not trust us, and that he will not like the way we express our intentions unless we have a better understanding of them. However, as the examples above reflect, as long as we focus on the feelings and needs of others, all criticisms, attacks, insults or ridicule will disappear. The more we do that, the more we can appreciate the simple fact that sometimes we feel that we have been blamed, and in fact that is the way others express their needs and requests. If we were aware of that, we would not consider ourselves to be harmed. On the contrary, if one looks at one's own or the other's faults, we think we're being devalued. The writer Joseph Campbell said, “In order to be happy, it is necessary to put aside the question of `what others think about me'. “When we see so-called criticisms and accusations as gifts from others — opportunities to serve people in distress, we feel this happiness.

p53.original: 如果人们常常怀疑我们的诚意，那么，我们就需要好好审视自己的动机。也许，我们只是在机械地运用非暴力沟通，而忘记其目的。这时，我们就可以问自己，我们关心的是加深与人的联系，还是以“标准的”非暴力沟通方式来说话。或者，虽然我们是以非暴力沟通的方式来表达自己，我们在乎的也许只是改变他人来迎合我们的需要。
p53.en: If people often question our sincerity, then we need to look at our motives. Perhaps we are simply mechanically using Nonviolent Communication to forget our purpose. At that point, we can ask ourselves whether we are concerned with deepening human ties or speaking in “standard” non-violent ways of communication. Or, while we express ourselves in a non-violent way of communication, what we care about is perhaps simply changing others to meet our needs.

p54.original: 有些人认为以非暴力沟通的方式来给他人反馈是在浪费时间。一位政府部门的主管在一个研讨班中谈到：“我的职责是说明事实和解决问题，不是为每个来找我的人提供心理咨询。”然而，许多来找他解决问题的市民，对他却十分不满。有几位市民后来悄悄告诉我：“你去他的办公室谈点事情，他就给你介绍一些情况，你无法知道他把你的话听进去了没有。于是，你就开始怀疑他的信息是否有助于解决问题。”给他人反馈是在节约而非浪费时间。关于劳资谈判的研究显示，如果双方同意在作出答复前先准确地重述对方的观点，那么，达成协议的时间将可以比平时缩短一半。
p54.en: Some people think it is a waste of time to give feedback to others in a non-violent way. In a seminar, the head of a government department said: “My job is to explain the facts and solve the problems, not to provide psychological counselling to everyone who comes to me. However, many of the citizens who came to him to solve the problem were disgruntled with him. Several citizens later whispered to me: “Go to his office and talk, and he will give you some information, and you cannot know whether he has listened to you. So you start to wonder if his message will help solve the problem. "The feedback to others is saving, not wasting, time. Studies on collective bargaining show that if both parties agree to re-state the views of the other party accurately before they respond, then the time for reaching an agreement will be reduced by half than normally.

p55.original: 我想起了另外一个例子。有一位先生在开始时也不认为给他人反馈有什么价值。有一段时间，他与太太的关系十分紧张，于是，他们一起参加了一个非暴力沟通研讨班。期间，太太对他说：“你从不好好听我讲话。”
p55.en: I've come up with another example. One gentleman did not see any value in giving feedback to others at the outset. For some time, his relationship with his wife was very tense, so they participated together in a Nonviolent Communication workshop. During that time, the wife said to him, "You never listen to me.

p58.original: 这时，我对这位先生说：“我担心你也许只是在证实她的观点。从她的反应来看，你的回答体现不出你在认真倾听她。”
p58.en: At this point, I said to the gentleman: “I'm afraid you may be just confirming her point of view. From her reaction, your answer does not reflect that you are listening to her carefully.

p59.original: 对我的观点，他有些困惑。于是，我问他是否可以让我来扮演他的角色。他很乐意我这么做。接着，我和他的太太就展开了以下的对话：
p59.en: He's a little confused about my point of view. So I asked him if I could play his role. He'd be happy to do it. Then I and his wife started the following conversation:

p60.original: 太太：“你从不好好听我讲话。”
p60.en: Ma'am: You never listen to me.

p61.original: 我：“听起来，你很失望。你需要体贴，是吗？”
p61.en: I said, "Sounds like you're disappointed. You need to be kind, don't you?

p62.original: 这位女士听到我的回答后，流下了眼泪。她终于得到了别人的理解。我转过身去，和她先生说：“我相信这就是她的需要——她需要倾听和理解。”这位先生十分惊讶：“她想要的只是这个？”他很难相信，这么简单一句话对他太太能有这么大的影响。
p62.en: When the lady heard my answer, she shed tears. She finally got the understanding. I turned around and said to her husband, “I believe that this is what she needs — she needs to listen and understand. "This gentleman is very surprised," she said. It's hard for him to believe that such a simple sentence can have such an impact on his wife.

p63.original: 在接下来的时间中，这位先生也就某件事表达了对太太的不满。当太太说出她所意识到的他的感受和需要时，他显得很高兴。他看着我说：“这是有价值的。”一旦一个人意识到自己得到了理解和接纳，一般来说，他会觉得很惬意。
p63.en: In the coming period, the gentleman also expressed his dissatisfaction with the wife for something. He was pleased when the wife spoke of the feelings and needs that she was aware of. And he looked at me and he said, "It's worth it. “When a person realizes that he has been understood and accepted, he generally feels comfortable.

p65.original: 我建议，在解决问题或询问他人的请求前，为他人的充分表达创造条件。如果过早地提及他人的请求，我们也许就无法传达我们的关心；甚至还会被看作是应付。而且，在谈话刚开始时，人们所表达的感受往往是冰山之一角，有许多相关的感受——通常是更为强烈的情感，并没有得到表达。倾听将为他们探究和表达内心深处的感受创造条件。反之，如果急于了解他们的请求或表达自己，就会妨碍这个过程。
p65.en: I suggest that the conditions be created for the full expression of others before solving their problems or asking questions about their requests. We may not be able to convey our concerns if we make premature references to requests from others; It'll even be seen as a response. Moreover, at the beginning of the conversation, the feelings expressed were often one of the tip of the iceberg, and there were many related feelings — usually stronger emotions — that were not expressed. Listening will create the conditions for them to explore and express their deep-seated feelings. Conversely, an eagerness to understand their requests or to express themselves would impede the process.

p66.original: 假定有一位母亲和我们说：“不知道怎么回事，我的孩子不论我和他说什么，他都不听。”这时，我们就可以表达我们的理解：“听起来，你很伤心，你希望找到和孩子沟通的办法。”这样的回答通常会鼓励对方去了解自己的感受和需要。如果我们的理解是准确的，这位母亲一般就会开始表达其他感受：“也许这是我的错。我总是冲他大喊大叫。”作为听众，我们继续体会她所表达的感受和需要，并给予反馈：“你希望你能多体贴孩子，以前没有做到这一点，你现在有些内疚，是吗？”如果这位母亲觉得我们能够理解她，她也许会接着说：“我是一个失败的母亲。”我们这时可以继续把我们的理解反馈给她：“你有些灰心，你想加深与孩子的感情联系，是吗？”就这样，我们一直保持关注，直到她充分表达相关的感受。
p66.en: Assuming a mother said to us: “I don't know what's going on, my child doesn't listen to me and him, no matter what I say to him. And then we can express our understanding: “You sound sad, you want to find a way to communicate with the children. Such answers usually encourage each other to understand their own feelings and needs. If our understanding is correct, the mother will generally begin to express other feelings: "Maybe it's my fault. I always yelled at him. As listeners, we continue to appreciate the feelings and needs that she expressed and to give feedback: “You want to be more sensitive to the child, you have not done so before, and you feel a little guilty now, have you? If the mother felt we could understand her, she might go on and say, “I am a failed mother. We can continue to feed her our understanding at this time: "You're a little frustrated, you want to deepen your relationship with the child, right? So, we stay focused until she fully expresses the relevant feelings.

p67.original: 怎样判断对方的感受是否已经充分表达呢？首先，如果一个人觉得别人已经完全明白他的意思，他就会变得轻松。这时，我们也会感到放松。另一个更为明显的标志是，他停止了谈话。如果无法确定对方是否还有话要说，就不妨问一句：“你还有什么话要告诉我吗？”
p67.en: How can one judge whether the other's feelings have been adequately expressed? First of all, if a person feels that others have fully understood his meaning, he becomes relaxed. And then we'll feel relaxed. Another more obvious sign is that he stopped talking. If it is not possible to determine if the other party has anything to say, ask: “Do you have anything else to tell me?

p68.original: 当我们痛苦得无法倾听
p68.en: When we're too painful to listen

p69.original: 我们无法给别人我们自己都没有的东西。有时，我们会发现自己没有心情去关心别人。一般来说，这反映了我们也需要得到关心。如果告诉他人我们正处于痛苦中，我们无法顾及他们的感受和需要，别人很可能就会伸出援手。
p69.en: We can't give people what we don't have. Sometimes we find ourselves not in the mood to care for others. In general, this reflects the attention that we also need. If we tell him that we are in pain and that we are unable to take their feelings and needs into account, it is likely that others will come to their aid.

p70.original: 然而，在许多时候，我们需要自己的体贴。联合国前秘书长汉马斯克德（Dag Hammarskjold）曾经说道：“你越是留意自己内心的声音，就越能够听到别人的声音。”一旦我们能够敏锐地察觉并照顾自己的感受和需要，我们就有能力迅速调整好状态，来倾听他人。如果做不到这一点，我们还有另外两种选择。
p70.en: However, in many cases, we need our own kindness. The former Secretary-General of the United Nations, Dag Hammarskjord, once said: “The more you look at the voices inside you, the more you can hear others. Once we are able to be sensitive and to take care of our feelings and needs, we have the capacity to quickly adjust our state to listen to others. If that is not possible, we have two other options.

p71.original: 其中一种选择是大声地提出请求。有一次，我应邀去协调两个帮派之间的矛盾。在冲突中，双方都有人死亡。最严重的一个月，一方死了两人，另一方死了一人。为了帮助他们倾听彼此的意见并找到解决冲突的办法，我紧张地工作了三天。在开车回家的路上，我感到筋疲力尽，我和自己说，我再也不想去协调任何冲突。
p71.en: One option was to make the request aloud. On one occasion, I was asked to reconcile the two gangs. During the conflict, there were deaths on both sides. In the worst month, two people died on one side and one on the other. I worked intensively for three days to help them listen to each other and find a solution to the conflict. I was exhausted on my way home, and I said to myself that I never wanted to coordinate any more conflicts.

p72.original: 可是，一到家，我就看到我的两个孩子在吵架。我没有力气去了解他们的情况，于是，我就大声地提出请求：“我很痛苦！我现在真的不想过问你们的事情！我需要安静！”我年仅九岁的大儿子停了下来，问道：“你愿意和我们说说吗？”我相信，如果我们能够直接地表达我们的痛苦，那么，即使对方也处于痛苦之中，有时他也能够意识到我们的需要。当然，我并不想冲着孩子大声地喊：“你们怎么回事？你们就不会乖一点吗？我在外面忙了一整天，还不够累吗？”我也不想说别的来指责孩子。我大声地提出请求，是为了提醒他们注意我此时此刻的痛苦和需要。
p72.en: But as soon as I got home, I saw my two kids fighting. I didn't have the strength to know about them, so I asked out loud, "I'm in pain! I really don't want to ask you anything right now! I need to be quiet! My first son, who was nine years old, stopped and asked, "Will you tell us about it? “I believe that if we can express our suffering directly, then even the other side is in pain, and sometimes he is aware of our needs. Of course, I don't want to shout at the kids, "What's wrong with you?" Wouldn't you guys be a little bit more good? I've been busy all day. Aren't I tired? "I don't want to say anything else to blame the children. I am making this plea out loud in order to remind them of the pain and needs of my time.

p73.original: 不过，如果对方正处于激烈的情绪中，他也可能无法留意我们的感受和需要。这时，我们的另一种选择是，换一个环境。我们需要时间和空间来调整状态，等平静下来了，再回来。
p73.en: However, if the other side is in a state of intense emotion, he may not be able to notice our feelings and needs. At that point, our alternative is to change the environment. We need time and space to adjust the situation, and when it calms down, we'll come back.

p75.original: 当他人遭遇不幸时，我们常常急于提建议，安慰，或表达我们的态度和感受。为了倾听他人，我们需要先放下已有的想法和判断，全心全意地体会对方。倾听他人有助于对他人的理解和接纳。
p75.en: When others suffer, we are often eager to come up with advice, comfort or express our attitudes and feelings. In order to listen to others, we need to put aside existing ideas and judgements and to feel each other with all our heart. Listening to others helps to understand and embrace others.

p76.original: 与此同时，不论别人用怎样的词语表达自己，我们都可以用心体会他们的观察、感受、需要和请求。有时，我们可以主动表达我们的理解，来帮助对方了解我们在何种程度上明白了他的意思。在交流的过程中，我们保持持续的关注，为对方的充分表达创造条件。
p76.en: At the same time, no matter what words others use to express themselves, we can feel their observations, feelings, needs and requests in our hearts. Sometimes, we can take the initiative to express our understanding to help each other understand the extent to which we understand what he means. In the course of our exchanges, we have maintained our constant attention and created the conditions for the full expression of each other.

p77.original: 当我们痛苦得无法倾听他人时，我们需要（1）体会自己的感受和需要；（2）大声地提出请求；（3）换一个环境。
p77.en: When we suffer too much to listen to others, we need (1) to feel our feelings and needs; (2) The request is made aloud; (3) A new environment.

p79.original: 一位先生临死前的谈话
p79.en: A conversation before a gentleman died.

p80.original: 有位病人已被诊断为肺癌晚期。在他被送往医院前，一位前来协助的护士以及他夫妇两人在他家中有了以下一段对话。谈话一开始，他太太就谈到了他们的家庭护士。
p80.en: One patient has been diagnosed as terminal lung cancer. Before he was taken to hospital, a nurse who came to assist him and the couple had the following conversation at his home. At the beginning of the conversation, his wife spoke about their family nurse.

p81.original: 太太：“她不是一位好护士。”

p82.original: 护士：（体会这位太太的感受和愿望）“你希望护士能够提供更好的服务？”
p82.en: Nurse: “Do you want the nurse to provide a better service?

p83.original: 太太：“她什么都没做。只要他的脉搏稍微快一些，她就让他停止走路。”
p83.en: Ma'am: She didn't do anything. As long as his pulse was a little faster, she stopped him walking.

p84.original: 护士：（继续体会她的感受和愿望）“他很少活动，你担心他无法恢复健康，是吗？”
p84.en: Nurse: “He rarely moves, you worry that he won't be able to recover, right?

p85.original: 太太：（哭了起来）“是的，我真的很害怕！”

p86.en: Nurse: "Are you afraid of losing him?

p87.original: 太太：“是的。我们一起生活了一辈子。”

p88.original: 护士：（注意了解她的其他感受）“你担心，如果有一天他走了，你将无依无靠？”
p88.en: Nurse: "You're worried that if he leaves one day you'll be helpless?

p89.original: 太太：“我无法想象，没有他，我怎么活下去。他总是在我身边。”
p89.en: Ma'am: I can't imagine how I'd survive without him. He's always around me.

p90.original: 护士：“所以，想到自己要一个人生活，你感到很凄凉。”
p90.en: Nurse: "So, you feel sad thinking about living alone.

p91.original: 太太：“除了他，没有人会和我生活在一起。你知道，他是我的全部。我女儿甚至都不和我说话。”
p91.en: Ma'am, "No one lives with me except him. You know, he's all I have. My daughter doesn't even talk to me.

p92.original: 护士：“想到你女儿，你似乎就很伤心，你希望你们的感情能好些？”
p92.en: Nurse: "You seem sad to think of your daughter, and you want your feelings to be better?"

p93.original: 太太：“是的。但她很自私。我不知道我为什么要生孩子？生孩子有什么好？！”
p93.en: Mrs. "Yes. But she's selfish. I don't know why I have to have a baby. What's good about having a baby? I don't know.

p94.original: 护士：“听起来，你很失望。在你先生病重的时候，你希望能有亲人在你身边。”
p94.en: Nurse: Sounds like you're disappointed. When your husband is very ill, you wish you had someone close to you.

p95.original: 太太：“他病得这么重，我不知道该怎么办才好……除了你，我甚至连一个说话的人都没有……他总是沉默不语……你看看，他一句话也没有！”（她先生仍保持着沉默）
p95.en: Ma'am, “He's so sick that I don't know what to do I don't even have a man to talk to except you he's always quiet and look, he's not saying a word! Her husband's still silent

p96.original: 护士：“你是说，在这困难的时刻，你希望你们两个能互相支持？”
p96.en: Nurse: "Are you saying that in this difficult time, you want the two of you to support each other?

p97.original: 太太：“是的。（她停了一下，然后，提了一个请求）我想请你用刚才谈话的方式和我先生谈谈。”
p97.en: Mrs. "Yes. I'd like you to talk to my husband in the way you just talked to him.

p98.original: 护士：（想了解这位太太的目的）“你希望他能说出自己的感受？”
p98.en: Nurse: "Do you want him to say what he feels?

p99.original: 太太：“是的，是的，就是这个意思！我希望他愿意讲几句。我想知道他现在的心情。”（通过护士的帮助，这位太太意识到自己的愿望并提出了明确的请求。这是很重要的，因为人们常常并不了解自己想要得到什么，即使他们知道自己不想要什么。我们看到一个明确的请求——“请你用刚才谈话的方式和我先生谈谈”——如何成为献给另一个人的礼物。护士现在就可以采取行动来满足这位太太的心愿。这改变了屋内的气氛——因为她们成为“同事”，开始“一起工作”。）
p99.en: Ma'am: Yes, yes, that's what it means! I hope he would like to say a few words. I want to know what he's feeling right now. “With the help of a nurse, the wife was aware of her wishes and made a clear request. This is important because people often do not know what they want, even if they know what they don't want. We see a clear request — “Please talk to my husband in the way you just spoke” — as a gift to someone else. The nurse can now take action to meet the wishes of the wife. This changed the atmosphere in the house — because they became “colleagues” and started “working together”. I don't think so.

p100.original: 护士：（转向那位先生）“听了你太太刚才和我的谈话，你现在感觉怎么样？”
p100.en: Nurse: "How do you feel now, when you hear your wife talking to me?

p102.original: 护士：“你愿意现在和她谈谈吗？”
p102.en: Nurse: Would you like to talk to her now?

p103.original: 先生：“是的，我们需要好好聊聊。”
p103.en: Sir: Yes, we need to talk.

p104.original: 护士：“你病得这么重，你愿意告诉她你的感受吗？”
p104.en: Nurse: "You're so sick, would you like to tell her how you feel?

p105.original: 先生：“感觉不太好。”（我们常用“好”或“坏”来描述感受。使用更为具体的词语，将有助于他太太更好地了解他的感受。）
p105.en: Sir: It doesn't feel good. “We often use the word “good” or “bad” to describe feelings. The use of more specific language would help his wife to better understand his feelings. I don't think so.

p106.original: 护士：（帮助他进一步表达感受）“你担心你的病治不好吗？”
p106.en: Nurse: "Do you worry about your illness?

p107.original: 先生：“不，我并不担心这个。”（注意：护士猜得不准确，并没有妨碍他们的交流。）
p107.en: Sir: No, I'm not worried about that. “Note: Nurses are inaccurate and do not prevent them from communicating. I don't think so.

p108.original: 护士：“生活变成这样，你感到恼怒吗？”（由于这位先生难以表达他的具体感受，护士就继续协助他。）
p108.en: Nurse: "Do you get angry with life being like this? The nurse continued to assist him because of his difficulty in expressing his specific feelings. I don't think so.

p110.original: 护士：（这时，她决定直接表达她的感受。）“我有些困惑，不知道你具体是怎样的感受。你可以说说吗？”
p110.en: Nurse: At this point, she decided to express her feelings directly. "I'm confused, I don't know how you feel. Can you say something?

p111.original: 先生：“我想，我是担心，我不在她身边，她怎么办。”
p111.en: Mr. “I think I was worried that I wasn't there for her, what would she do?

p112.original: 护士：“你担心她无法独自面对生活？”
p112.en: Nurse: "Are you worried that she can't face life alone?

p113.original: 先生：“是的。我怕她没有勇气活下去。”
p113.en: Sir: Yes. I'm afraid she doesn't have the courage to live.

p114.original: 护士：（她知道临死的病人常常因为惦记亲人而放心不下。有时，病人需要他的亲人告诉他，他们准备好了面对他的死亡——这样，他才可以放心地离去。）“你是否想知道你太太现在的心情？”
p114.en: Nurse: “She knows that dying patients are often worried about their loved ones. Sometimes patients need his relatives to tell him that they are ready to face his death — so that he can leave without fear. "Do you want to know what your wife is feeling now?

p116.original: 这时，他太太加入了谈话。当着护士的面，他们开始亲切地交谈。在上述的对话中，太太开始时表达的是对家庭护士的不满。随着对话的深入，她意识到，在这人生的艰难时刻，她极为渴望加强与先生的联系。
p116.en: At that point, his wife joined the conversation. In front of the nurses, they started to talk with kindness. During the above-mentioned dialogue, the wife began by expressing dissatisfaction with the family nurse. As the dialogue advanced, she realized that she was keen to strengthen her ties with Mr. S. at this difficult time in her life.

p117.original: 练习五 倾听他人并给予反馈
p117.en: Practice five, listen to others and give feedback.

p118.original: 以下是甲和乙的十组对话。请问，在哪些对话中，乙用心体会甲的感受和需要并给予反馈？
p118.en: Below are the 10 sets of dialogues for A and B. In which dialogues does ZE feel the feelings and needs of A and give them feedback?

p119.original: 1.甲：“我又误机了，我真是个混蛋！”
p119.en: "I missed my flight again. I'm such an asshole!

p120.original: 乙：“没有人是十全十美的，不要太严格要求自己。”
p120.en: B: “No one is perfect, and don't be too demanding.

p121.original: 2.甲：“我认为我们应该把这些非法移民遣送回国。”
p121.en: 2. A: “I think we should repatriate these illegal immigrants.

p122.original: 乙：“这对改善社会治安有帮助吗？”
p122.en: b: “Is this helping to improve public security?

p123.en: A: “Do you think you know everything? I don't know.

p124.original: 乙：“听起来，你有些不耐烦，因为你希望每个人的意见都能得到倾听？ ”
p124.en: B: “Does it sound like you're a little impatient because you want everyone's views to be heard?

p125.original: 4.甲：“你从不把我当回事。要不是我帮你，你自己一个人能处理这么多事情吗？”
p125.en: A: “You never took me seriously. If I hadn't helped you, would you be able to handle all this by yourself?

p126.original: 乙：“你怎么能这样想！我一直都很尊重你。”
p126.en: B: How can you think that! I've always respected you.

p127.original: 5.甲：“你怎么可以那样和我说话？”
p127.en: "How can you talk to me like that?"

p128.original: 乙：“我那样说话，你是不是很伤心？”
p128.en: B: Is it sad that I talk like that?

p129.original: 6.甲：“想到我先生，我就有些气恼。我需要他的时候，他总是不在我身边。”
p129.en: 6.A: “I have a bit of anger when I think of my husband. I need him when he's not around.

p130.original: 乙：“你是希望他多陪陪你？”
p130.en: B: You want him to be with you?

p131.original: 7.甲：“我真受不了我自己，我现在变得这么胖！”
p131.en: "I can't stand myself, I'm so fat!"

p133.original: 8.甲：“我紧张地筹备女儿的婚礼。可是，我亲家老是有新主意，真烦！”
p133.en: A: “I was nervous about preparing my daughter's wedding. But I've always had new ideas. It's annoying!

p134.original: 乙：“听起来，你有些着急，你希望能得到理解与配合，是吗？”
p134.en: B: “You sound a little anxious, you want to get along with it, don't you?

p135.original: 9.甲：“如果亲戚来之前不和我打招呼，我真的不想接待他们。”
p135.en: “If relatives do not greet me before coming, I really do not want to receive them.

p136.original: 乙：“我知道这是什么感觉。我也这样。”
p136.en: B: I know what it feels like. Me too.

p137.original: 10.甲：“你的表现让我很失望。我本来指望你们部门上个月的产出能够翻番。”
p137.en: A: “Your performance has disappointed me. I would have expected your department to double its output last month.

p138.original: 乙：“我知道你很失望。但上个月我们部门请病假的人很多。”
p138.en: B: I know you're disappointed. But last month we had a lot of sick leave calls from our department.

p139.original: 以下是我对练习5的看法：
p139.en: Here's what I think about practice 5:

p140.original: 1.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不一致。因为我认为乙是在安慰。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“你很失望，是因为你希望能够信赖自己，是吗？”
p140.en: 1. If you choose this dialogue, we are divided. Because I think the b is comforting. If B. listens with his heart and gives his feedback, he might say, "You're disappointed because you want to be able to trust yourself, right?

p141.original: 2.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不一致。因为我认为乙是在询问。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“你有些担心，因为你很看重社会秩序和安全？”
p141.en: 2. If you choose this dialogue, we are not in agreement. Because I think the ab is asking. And if he listens with his heart and gives his feedback, he might say, “You're worried because you value social order and security?

p142.original: 3.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见一致。
p142.en: If you choose this dialogue, we agree.

p143.original: 4.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不一致。我认为乙是在辩解。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“你好像有些失落，你希望得到欣赏和肯定？”
p143.en: 4. If you choose this dialogue, we are not in agreement. I think B is defending. If Zelig listens and gives his feedback, he might say, “You seem to be a bit lost, and you want to be appreciated and confirmed?

p144.original: 5.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不一致。我认为乙是在为甲的感受负责。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“听起来，你很伤心，因为你需要体贴？”
p144.en: 5. If you choose this dialogue, we are not in agreement. I think B is responsible for A's feelings. If B. listens and gives feedback, he might say, "Sounds like you're sad because you need to be kind?

p145.original: 6.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不完全一致。我认为乙将甲的想法反馈给了甲。然而，我相信，反馈感受和需要更能促进人与人的联系。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“听起来，你有些失落，因为你需要支持与关心？”
p145.en: 6. If you choose this dialogue, we are not entirely in agreement. I think the idea of A is fed back to A. However, I believe that feedback and the need to promote people-to-people contacts are more conducive. If B. listens and gives feedback, he might say, “Does it sound like you're a little lost, because you need support and care?

p146.original: 7.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不一致。我认为乙是在提建议。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“你对自己好像有些不耐烦，你很看重健康，是吗？”
p146.en: 7. If you choose this dialogue, we are divided. I think B is making a suggestion. And if he listens with his heart and gives his feedback, he might say, "You seem a little impatient with yourself, and you value your health, right?

p147.original: 8.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见一致。
p147.en: If you choose this dialogue, we agree.

p148.original: 9.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不一致。我认为乙是在表示同情。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“你是不是有些厌烦，你希望你的需要也能得到尊重，是吗？”
p148.en: 9. If you choose this dialogue, we are not in agreement. I think B is expressing sympathy. If Zelig listens and gives feedback, he might say, “Are you a little tired and you want your needs to be respected, too, right?

p149.original: 10.如果你选择这个对话，我们意见不一致。我认为，虽然乙提到了甲的感受，但乙主要是在辩解。如果乙用心倾听并给予反馈，他也许会说：“你看来很失望，你看重工作效率，是吗？”
p149.en: 10. If you choose this dialogue, we are not in agreement. I think that while B mentions the feeling of A, B is primarily a justification. If B. listens and gives feedback, he might say, "You look disappointed, you look at efficiency, right?
